# Swift's Final Farewell

After 22 years watching the universe through ultraviolet, X-ray, and gamma-ray eyes, NASA's Swift Observatory made a spectacular final journey, burning up like a shooting star over Indonesia in November 2024. The telescope's incredible legacy lives on through millions of images it captured of the cosmos's most violent and energetic events—exploding stars and supermassive black holes—providing scientists with unprecedented details about the universe's most extreme phenomena.
